topic: Bind asynchronous applicant reconciliation to its observed issuance transaction
observedProblem: sync_issuance captured the current transaction ID before an asynchronous issuer GET, but passed only application ID and returned status into the mutation.
A concurrently completed operator reissue replaced the transaction and offer while that old GET remained in flight.
The old revoked response then expired the replacement offer; the old issued response marked the replacement offer and applicant credentialed, despite the replacement transaction still being pending.

httpBranchesCarryTheObservedBinding: absent, empty or local transaction ID without remote read
implementation.preservedBehavior: Matching current transaction responses retain existing status and expiry reconciliation semantics. There is no new remote request, cancellation, issuance, or revocation side effect.
implementation.sharedRustGuard: HTTP adapters pass the observed binding; the shared ApplicantService method performs the comparison and all permitted mutations under one write lock.

focusedProof: The issuer fixture blocks an actual HTTP transaction read; the real operator /issue route completes a replacement through the real service and a controlled FlowProvider; then the old HTTP response is released.
Both stale revoked and stale issued responses return the replacement OFFERED/OFFER_READY DTO, preserve the whole store and timestamps, and perform zero additional persistence writes.
Current revoked and issued responses still produce the established EXPIRED and CLAIMED projections and persist normally.
Absent, empty, local and prior remote transaction bindings are checked before local expiry; the matching current binding can still expire the offer normally.

executionEnvironment.loopbackApproval: Automatic review permitted the focused test processes to bind ephemeral localhost listeners. No approval rejection or live-service contact occurred.

followupExplanation: Four applicant files from the previous claim evidence subsequently changed in this separately committed reconciliation repair. Their final hashes are recorded here, and the final 42-test run repeats all previous 38 applicant cases.
remainingBoundaries: This guard discards a response for a different transaction after replacement; existing reconciliation behavior for the same transaction remains unchanged.
The change does not make transaction cancellation and operator reissue one atomic operation. Exact owned old/new transaction proof remains required in demo helpers.
No deployment, live beta flow, physical or native wallet, external Canvas delivery, resource cleanup, or real credential issuance was exercised.
